ai.definition: Inertial confinement fusion (ICF) uses powerful lasers to compress a tiny spherical fuel pellet, causing the fuel to reach conditions where nuclear fusion can occur.
ai.howItWorks: High-intensity laser beams are precisely aimed at a small capsule containing fusion fuel. The lasers heat and compress the fuel, causing it to ignite in a process similar to a supernova explosion, leading to a short-lived but intense fusion reaction.
ai.problemSolved: ICF addresses the challenge of achieving sustained nuclear fusion reactions that produce more energy than is required to initiate them, which would be necessary for practical fusion power generation.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves creating and testing laser systems capable of delivering precise, high-intensity pulses. Fuel capsules are also carefully engineered to ensure they can withstand the intense conditions without disintegrating prematurely.
ai.buildProcess: ICF facilities require sophisticated laser systems, vacuum chambers, and highly controlled environments. The fuel pellets must be precisely manufactured from materials like deuterium-tritium ice or lithium-deuteride.
ai.costDrivers: High costs are driven by the need for extremely powerful lasers, precise manufacturing of fuel capsules, and maintaining a clean, high-vacuum environment to prevent contamination.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: promising but with significant technical challenges remaining before practical applications can be realized
ai.regulation: Currently, there are no specific regulations for ICF research, but safety and environmental standards will likely increase as the technology moves towards commercialization.
ai.risks: Technical risks include achieving stable ignition conditions, maintaining laser precision over long periods, and ensuring safe handling of radioactive materials. Economic risks stem from the high cost of equipment and ongoing R&D funding.
ai.profitability: Not yet profitable; research and development are currently funded through government grants and private investment in fusion startups.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments will likely focus on improving laser systems, fuel capsule designs, and overall reactor efficiency to achieve net energy gain consistently and at lower costs.

glossary.def: The condition where the energy produced by a fusion reaction exceeds the energy required to initiate it.
A method of achieving nuclear fusion by compressing a fuel target using an external source of energy, such as laser beams or particle beams.

subsystems.name: Laser driver
subsystems.role: generates and amplifies the precisely shaped pulses that crush the fuel capsule.

subsystems.name: Beam transport and final optics
subsystems.role: routes and focuses every beam onto the target with micrometre precision.

subsystems.name: Target assembly
subsystems.role: the fuel capsule and the hohlraum that turns laser light into X-rays.

subsystems.name: Target chamber and positioner
subsystems.role: holds the target at the exact focus of all beams.

subsystems.name: Diagnostics and control
subsystems.role: measures how well the implosion performed and keeps the laser aligned.

subsystems.name: Power conversion (future plant)
subsystems.role: in a reactor, captures heat, breeds tritium and makes electricity.

buildSteps.title: Make the laser glass
buildSteps.detail: Neodymium-doped phosphate glass is melted, cast into large slabs and polished to optical flatness.

buildSteps.title: Build amplifier chains
buildSteps.detail: Slabs are stacked between flashlamps in long beamlines that amplify a small seed pulse to megajoules.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the target
buildSteps.detail: A hollow capsule is formed, filled with deuterium–tritium, and cooled until the fuel freezes into a smooth solid layer; the hohlraum is machined around it.

buildSteps.title: Align the system
buildSteps.detail: All 192 beams are aligned to hit the hohlraum symmetrically, and the target is positioned to within micrometres.

buildSteps.title: Fire the shot
buildSteps.detail: The lasers fire; inside the hohlraum they convert to X-rays that ablate the capsule, imploding the fuel until it ignites and releases fusion energy.

buildSteps.title: Move to repetition (future)
buildSteps.detail: A power plant would inject new targets several times per second instead of firing a few shots per day.

buildSteps.title: Capture heat and breed tritium
buildSteps.detail: A liquid-metal blanket absorbs fusion neutrons, breeds tritium from lithium, and carries heat away.

buildSteps.title: Generate electricity
buildSteps.detail: The captured heat drives a steam turbine and generator, as in a conventional power station.

prerequisites.why: the driver must deliver megajoules in a carefully tailored pulse to compress the fuel evenly.
the fuel layer must be near-perfect and kept at cryogenic temperature until the moment of firing.
scientific net energy gain was reached at the National Ignition Facility in 2022, but only once and with modest gain.
a power plant needs many shots per second, not a few per day.
the reaction consumes tritium and damages the chamber, so a plant must make its own fuel and survive neutron bombardment.

pathway.milestone: laser facilities such as the National Ignition Facility study ignition and measure gain
pathway.unlocks: confidence that inertial fusion can release more energy than the laser delivers.

pathway.milestone: higher gain and repeatable ignition with different target designs
pathway.unlocks: the physics basis for an engineering test facility.

pathway.milestone: engineering test facilities with high-repetition lasers and target injection
pathway.unlocks: proof that targets can be mass-produced and fired continuously.
electricity from inertial fusion, if tritium breeding and chamber materials are solved.
firm, low-carbon power alongside magnetic fusion and renewables.
